title: HttpService
summary: Web requests from your game: GetAsync/PostAsync/RequestAsync to external APIs, plus JSONEncode/JSONDecode for structured data. Requires 'Allow HTTP Requests' enabled; never call roblox.com domains.

methods.name: GetAsync
methods.description: HTTP GET; returns the response body as a string. Errors on non-2xx or network failure — wrap in pcall.

methods.name: PostAsync
methods.signature: HttpService:PostAsync(url: string, data: string, contentType?: Enum.HttpContentType) --> string
methods.description: HTTP POST with a string body.

methods.name: RequestAsync
methods.signature: HttpService:RequestAsync(options: { Url, Method?, Headers?, Body? }) --> { Success, StatusCode, StatusMessage, Headers, Body }
methods.description: Full-control request: method, headers, body. Returns a response table instead of erroring on bad status.

methods.name: JSONEncode / JSONDecode
methods.signature: HttpService:JSONEncode(value: any) --> string / HttpService:JSONDecode(json: string) --> any
methods.description: Convert Luau tables ↔ JSON strings. The standard JSON tooling even outside HTTP.

methods.name: GenerateGUID
methods.description: Random unique ID string — handy for request/record IDs.

methods.name: UrlEncode
methods.description: URL-escape a string for query parameters.

details.heading: Restrictions
details.body: Game setting 'Allow HTTP Requests' must be ON. Requests to *.roblox.com and other Roblox domains are blocked. Rate limited (~500 requests/minute per server; bursts throttled). Server-side recommended — client HTTP has tighter limits and can be spied on.

details.heading: Errors
details.body: GetAsync/PostAsync throw on failure (404, timeouts, throttling) — always pcall. RequestAsync returns Success=false instead of throwing.

explanation.whatItIs: Your game's phone line to the outside web: fetch data from your own backend, post to services, parse JSON — with Roblox guarding what numbers you can dial.
explanation.whyItExists: Games often need external systems: custom leaderboards, Discord announcements, AI services, cross-game data you control.
whenToUse: Talking to YOUR OWN backend/APIs you operate
JSONEncode/Decode for any structured data (DataStores, message payloads)
Webhooks (e.g., logging) — respecting their rate limits
RequestAsync when you need headers (auth tokens) or non-GET/POST verbs
whenNotToUse: Fetching arbitrary websites or untrusted URLs — validate every URL server-side
High-frequency polling — budgets are limited; cache results
Anything that could be a DataStore instead — built-in storage is simpler and safer
Never send secrets to the client; do authenticated calls from the server
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
server script ──pcall──▶ HttpService:GetAsync(url)
                              │
                    external API answers (JSON string)
                              │
                    JSONDecode → Luau table
```
Always: pcall it, decode defensively, retry with backoff.
tips: pcall + retry loop, same pattern as DataStores
RequestAsync returns a response TABLE — inspect .Success and .StatusCode
Cache aggressively; treat the HTTP budget as precious
commonMistakes: Forgetting to enable 'Allow HTTP Requests' — every call errors 403
Calling roblox.com endpoints — blocked by design
Doing HTTP inside RenderStepped/Heartbeat without throttling
Trusting JSONDecode output shapes without validation

examples.title: Robust GET with retries
examples.code:
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")

local function getJson(url, attempts)
    for i = 1, attempts do
        local ok, response = pcall(function()
            return HttpService:GetAsync(url)
        end)
        if ok then
            return HttpService:JSONDecode(response)
        end
        warn(`HTTP attempt {i} failed: {response}`)
        task.wait(2 ^ i)   -- exponential backoff
    end
    return nil
end

local data = getJson("https://api.example.com/status", 3)
if data then
    print("Status:", data.status)
end

examples.title: RequestAsync with headers
examples.code:
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")

local response = HttpService:RequestAsync({
    Url = "https://api.example.com/save",
    Method = "POST",
    Headers = { ["Authorization"] = "Bearer " .. API_TOKEN, ["Content-Type"] = "application/json" },
    Body = HttpService:JSONEncode({ coins = 100 }),
})

if response.Success then
    print("Saved. Status:", response.StatusCode)
else
    warn("Failed:", response.StatusCode, response.StatusMessage)
end
